weightedPrototype.whatItIs: The graybox rebuilt a static shape per state, so no render it produced was evidence about skinning. This binds the same authored bodies through the released binding pipeline - donor-measured armature, one vertex group per donor bone, normalised influences, Armature modifier, FBX export - and moves them by posing bones only.

weightedPrototype.exportVerified: Every variant written to FBX and read back: 40 bones, zero unweighted vertices, influence sums exactly 1.000, at most 2 influences per vertex (3 for the damped weighting) against Unity's 4, Armature modifier present.
weightedPrototype.brachiosaurusNeckDecision: NOT DECIDED. Owner correction of 2026-10-16: the Head-only weighting is a tested experimental CONTROL, not an approved shipping design, and this entry previously recorded it as decided. Three states, measurements preserved: the rigid control is stable under the tested probes - with the caveat that a neck which no longer answers to the probed joints cannot prove articulation by surviving them; the full and damped old-donor-pivot weightings FAILED at the recorded probes (3.46 visible stretch and 10.51 units of displacement; surface collapse to 0.14 of rest length); an acceptable articulated production design is NOT YET ESTABLISHED. These four rows varied weight distribution while keeping the donor's pivots, so they do not exhaust the permitted approaches and are not a proof that one rigid driver is the only possibility.
weightedPrototype.seamTreatment: Five weightings measured on the Elephant, visible-surface stretch. add_tube's default blend carries the limb socket OUT of the torso under a slam (hull 1.22). Pinning keeps it in and makes one band absorb the whole step (2.01). Graded rings fix the limb (1.52) and worsen the neck (gore 1.29 -> 1.58). Grading along the donor's own UpperTorso-Neck-Head chain was tried on the anatomy and LOST (1.72, and the curl floor from 0.84 to 0.13). Shipped: graded limb sockets, pinned neck anchor.
weightedPrototype.islandDefectClosed: The independent review had measured 18 to 52 px of background between torso and chain. Measured against a scale instead: the anchor ring sits 0.205 (Brachiosaurus) and 0.075 (Elephant) from the nearest torso vertex, against torso facet spacings of 0.707 and 0.684 - 0.29 and 0.11 of one facet - and it is pinned to UpperTorso, so those numbers are identical in every pose and cannot be reopened by motion.
weightedPrototype.definingMotion: Elephant trunk: bind-faithful, every chain bone exactly on the skin it drives, within tolerance to 12 deg/joint after the taper correction (was 8), 1.37 at 16; tusk-to-trunk clearance 0.113 at bind and 0.128 to 0.137 under curl, never touching. Brachiosaurus neck: rigid on Head, gore swing moves the skull 3.24 units at 1.20 visible stretch. Slam lifts one forefoot to +0.741 with the other three measuring exactly 0.000 above the sole plane.
weightedPrototype.topologyMetricCorrected: The earlier report counted faces pointing away from the WHOLE body's centroid, which labels the inner surface of every leg as inward and reported 78 and 105 on bodies with nothing wrong. Replaced by per-shell signed volume, which is exact: 8 shells (Brachiosaurus) and 12 (Elephant), 0 open, 0 inside out.

boundedArticulationExperiment.why: The four weightings all redistributed influence over the DONOR's existing pivots and none of them moved one. The owner's correction of 2026-10-16 required attacking the pivot instead, in one bounded, production-compatible experiment with explicit source and target frames stated before running.
boundedArticulationExperiment.mapping: SOURCE: the donor forward-chain bones' rotation relative to their own rest pose - what a clip animates and what survives a retarget; a raw local quaternion would not, because the rest orientations differ. TARGET: seven private drivers KMG_BrachioNeck_01..07 with heads on the authored neck's joints, driver 1 parented to the donor Head. MAP: driver k applies donor chain bone k's rest-relative rotation in driver k's own rest frame. UNCHANGED: the donor's body, shoulder, leg and tail motion, because the chain hangs off Head; no donor mesh, transform, clip or skeleton asset; no global bind pose.
boundedArticulationExperiment.result: Lever arms fall from 3.288 units and 3.06x to 0.000 and 0.00x. Under the 16 deg/joint chain probe the retargeted neck moves 3.73 against the control's 1.19, and every joint turns 15-21 degrees where the control's internal turns stay at their rest values. Visible stretch 1.269 at 8 deg/joint and 1.543 at 16 - the Elephant trunk's own figures, i.e. the authored neck now behaves like a chain whose bones sit on it. Both variants answer identically to a shoulder swing (3.100 at 1.203), so neither passed by ignoring a probe.

weightedPrototype.evidenceLevelsKeptApart: 1 unchanged base vertex coordinates during a posed experiment; 2 the evaluated Armature modifier's deformation; 3 FBX round-trip bone and weight integrity; 4 correct runtime binding - NOT established; 5 actual native animation, contacts and appearance - NOT established. None of 1-3 establishes 4 or 5.
weightedPrototype.rigidDistortionRelabelled: It was named as though it proved the deformation matched the bone that drives it. It does not: it is the largest change in a vertex's distance to its part's centroid, invariant under rotation, so a part driven by the wrong bone passes unchanged. Now documented as that, with a direct check beside it - the skull against pose.matrix * bone.matrix_local^-1 * v in the armature space the modifier works in. GreaterOverrun.components: Two mechanical and four selection-time prerequisites. Mechanical: ManeuverProvokeAttack(Overrun) and ManeuverBonus(Overrun, +2). Prerequisites: Strength 13, BaseAttackBonus 6, PrerequisiteFeature(PowerAttackFeature) and PrerequisiteFeature(ImprovedOverrunFeature).
GreaterOverrun.whoProvokesFromWhomOnWhichEvent: Read from the IL of ManeuverProvokeAttack, not inferred from its name. The type extends RuleInitiatorLogicComponent<RuleCombatManeuver> and subscribes as IInitiatorRulebookHandler, so it is the initiator’s feat that owns it. OnEventAboutToTrigger is empty (a bare ret). OnEventDidTrigger is: if (evt.Type == this.ManeuverType) and evt.Success, then Game.Instance.CombatEngagementController.ProvokeAttackOfOpportunity(evt.Target). So the party that provokes is the maneuver’s TARGET, not the initiator; it happens after the maneuver resolves, and only on success. That matches the printed Greater Overrun rider exactly. It does not touch the rule’s IsGreater flag.
GreaterOverrun.maneuverBonusConsumer: ManeuverBonus extends RuleInitiatorLogicComponent<RuleCalculateCMB>, so the +2 applies only while a CMB is being calculated for the initiator.
GreaterOverrun.trampleConsumerClaimWithdrawn: WITHDRAWN as false. This ledger previously inferred a real consumer because ConfigureUngulateTrample clones native OverrunAbility 1a3b471ecea51f7439a946b23577fd70. Clone ancestry did not establish the configured graph’s behaviour, exactly as warned. The IL of AbilityCustomOverrun.<Deliver>d__9 branches on AutoSuccess BEFORE it constructs anything: if AutoSuccess is true it jumps past the "new RuleCombatManeuver(caster, target, Overrun)" and its context.TriggerRule call entirely. ExpandedSummoningSpecialBuilder sets overrun.AutoSuccess = true for every shipped trample. So a trample raises neither RuleCombatManeuver nor RuleCalculateCMB, and NEITHER Greater Overrun component can fire through trample.

Nothing was added to trample to manufacture a consumer: no maneuver check, no +2 to trample damage or DC, no change to its response options, and no forced knockdown or provocation.
GreaterOverrun.prerequisiteFinding: Answered separately, as required. PrerequisiteFeature and PrerequisiteStatValue derive from Prerequisite : BlueprintComponent and declare ZERO rulebook handlers, so they act only during feat selection in the level-up system. A direct blueprint grant bypasses them, and they have no effect during use. The missing Improved Overrun therefore would not block a direct grant of Greater Overrun, and no extra feat and no stat-block rewrite is needed to avoid the discrepancy.

implementation.noDuplicateProvocation: The native feat is cloned, not granted: its ManeuverProvokeAttack fires on evt.Success alone, which provokes for an ordinary pass-through and for a target that cannot be knocked off at all. implementation.knockdownCorrection: Read from IL, not assumed: AbilityCustomOverrun stores !Success in V_5 and IL_03b1 branches to the Actions block only when it is false, so that list runs once per overrun target, in that target's data scope, and only on a successful maneuver. The native overrun ability ships the list EMPTY, which is why nothing in this build ever knocked an overrun target prone and why the printed Greater Overrun rider could not fire. This creature's own command now carries one ContextActionKnockdownTarget. That action's own IL supplies the controls rather than this project inventing them: UnitHelper.CanBeKnockedOff gates eligibility, Descriptor.State.Prone.ShouldBeActive is the native prone state so an already-prone target stays prone, and IKnockOffHandler.HandleKnockOff is raised on the native EventBus. One action, one ability, no global rule, and Trample - AutoSuccess true, its own action lists - gains nothing.
implementation.thresholdCorrection: The printed rule knocks a target prone only when the overrun result beats its CMD by 5 or more, and Greater Overrun's rider follows THAT knockdown. The engine already draws the line and this reads its answer rather than computing a second one: RuleCombatManeuver.SuccesValue is InitiatorCMValue - TargetCMD, and IsPartialSuccess is Success && Type == Overrun && SuccesValue < 5, against the engine's own OverrunPartialSuccessThreshold of 5. actionAndMovementContract.question: The command is configured DoubleMove, Standard with IsFullRoundAction, while the printed ordinary maneuver is a standard action taken during your move or as part of a charge. Reviewed on the engine's actual behaviour rather than on the flags.
actionAndMovementContract.whatTheILShows: AbilityCustomOverrun really moves the caster and really bounds it: the delivery accumulates passedDistance from the caster's position each step and compares it against maxDistance, continuing only while passedDistance < maxDistance. Movement is therefore accounted for by the engine, not simulated by this project.
actionAndMovementContract.finding: FAITHFUL AS THE CHARGE FORM, no change made. DoubleMove plus a full-round cost is the engine expressing 'move up to double speed and do this en route', which is exactly the printed 'as part of a charge' branch, and it never costs the creature LESS than the printed 'standard action during your move'. The cheaper alternative - standard action, not full round, still DoubleMove - would hand the creature a double move and keep its move action, which is an unapproved action-cost adaptation in its favour. No new action or movement system was built.
actionAndMovementContract.targetCountDefectFound: CORRECTED. The command had FirstTargetOnly = false, copied from the trample shape it was cloned beside. The IL is unambiguous: with it false the delivery keeps enumerating Game.Instance.State.Units and overruns EVERY creature on the path; with it true, the moment overrunUnits is non-empty it branches to the movement accumulator, so the creature keeps moving and overruns nobody else. Printed ordinary Overrun is 'you can attempt to overrun your target, moving through its square' - one target. With the knockdown now implemented, the old setting would have knocked down every creature along a double-move path and made each provoke. Set to true on this command only; Trample keeps false, because trampling everything in the path is what Trample is.
